REWARD_MACHINE:
STATES: u0, u1, u2, u3, u4
INITIAL_STATE: u0
FINAL_STATES: u4
TRANSITION_FUNCTION:
(u0, blocker_moved & !has_door_key) -> u1
(u0, else) -> u0
(u1, has_door_key & blocker_moved) -> u2
(u1, else) -> u1
(u2, door_open) -> u3
(u2, key_lost) -> u2
(u2, else) -> u2
(u3, target_picked_up) -> u4
(u3, else) -> u3
(u4, else) -> u4
REWARD_FUNCTION:
(u0, blocker_moved & !has_door_key, u1) -> 0.2
(u1, has_door_key & blocker_moved, u2) -> 0.2
(u2, door_open, u3) -> 0.3
(u2, key_lost, u2) -> -0.3
(u3, target_picked_up, u4) -> 1.0
feedback: Accepted. Format: all required header fields are present in the paper's artifact layout (REWARD_MACHINE, STATES, INITIAL_STATE, FINAL_STATES, TRANSITION_FUNCTION, REWARD_FUNCTION); FINAL_STATES is nonempty, u4 is declared in STATES and is the true accepting condition (mission box picked up, which terminates the episode). Semantic fidelity: the RM structurally enforces every hard ordering the task states — u0->u1 only on blocker_moved (the !has_door_key guard is redundant, since the agent cannot hold the key and pick up the ball, but harmless), u1->u2 requires has_door_key together with the blocker still moved (meaningful: it correctly handles the ball being dropped back in front of the door), and u2->u3->u4 sequences door_open before target_picked_up, consistent with the environment's impossibility constraints. The soft constraint is explicit: key_lost is a self-loop regression in u2 with -0.3, the machine stays in u2 so the agent can re-acquire the key and still open the door (no deadlock), and key_lost is used as the one-step event it is, not as a latch. In u3 a post-opening key drop correctly produces no event (key_lost requires a closed door), matching the example trace's step-19 drop. Coverage: every state has a per-state else self-loop, so turns/moves, no-ops, and events irrelevant or impossible in that state (door_open in u0/u1, target_picked_up in u0-u2, key_lost in u3/u4 since the door cannot be relocked) are absorbed; all transition conditions are predicate-only, with no raw action names. Reward safety: progress rewards are dense, bounded, and monotone (0.2, 0.2, 0.3, 1.0) with a -0.3 penalty; there are no backward transitions, so no progress reward can be re-farmed, and the negative penalty gives no farming incentive. Minor, non-blocking leniency: key_lost can also occur in u0 (agent takes the key before moving the ball, then must drop it) and in u1 (agent re-blocks the door cell, picks up the key, then must drop it to free its hands); those occurrences fall into unpunished else self-loops. Both require the agent to already be off the sanctioned path, and the RM withholds all progress rewards until the correct order is re-established, so the optimal policy is unaffected; adding -0.3 key_lost self-loops in u0 and u1 would tighten fidelity but is not required by the task as stated.

feedback: All five environment-declared propositions are implemented and there are no extra functions. `blocker_moved` scans for the unique door and checks the cell immediately in front of it on the start side (door.x - 1, door.y), which is exactly the reference check at (dx - 1, dy): it is false only when a ball sits on that cell, true when the ball is carried (the cell is empty) or dropped elsewhere, and false again if the ball is dropped back there — the non-latching condition semantics. Since the environment has exactly one door located in the interior shared wall (x >= 1), the door-relative pair scan is equivalent to the reference cell check, and the x range starting at 1 keeps grid.get(x - 1, y) in bounds. `has_door_key` matches the reference: carrying a key whose color matches the scanned door, with short-circuit guarding of env.carrying. `door_open` matches the reference scan for an open door. `target_picked_up` matches the reference: carrying a box whose color is named by env.mission, so it adapts to the random mission color. `key_lost` correctly implements the event: it requires previous_valuation['has_door_key'] true, the has_door_key expression false now, and door_open false now, so it fires for one step after a drop of the key while the door is closed and never co-occurs with has_door_key or door_open; it reads env.episode_memory['previous_valuation'] only, and the extra None/missing-key guards are harmless because the first-step valuation has all propositions false, so the event is false at step 1 under both readings. All code is syntactically valid, uses no imports, performs no actions, mutates neither the environment nor episode memory, and guards every grid.get and env.carrying access against None before attribute reads.
